Lu. 18, 18.''}}* Good Mai{{ls}}ter, vvhat {{ls}}hal I doe that I may receiue life euerla{{ls}}ting? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=18}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to him, Why calle{{ls}}t thou me good? {{sup|‖}} None is good but one, God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=19}} Thou knovve{{ls}}t the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Note that the keeping of Gods cōmaundements procureth life euerla{{ls}}ting.}}∷ commaundements, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 13.''}}* ''Commit not aduoutrie, Kil not, Steale not, Beare not fal{{ls}}e vvitne{{ls}}{{ls}}e, doe no fraude, Honour thy father and mother''. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=20}} But he an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid to him, Mai{{ls}}ter al the{{ls}}e things I haue ob{{ls}}erued from my youth. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=21}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} beholding him, loued him, and {{ls}}aid to him, One thing is vvanting vnto thee: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This is coun{{ls}}el of perfectiō (not a precept) which the Religious profe{{ls}}{{ls}}ing and keeping voluntary pouertie, doe folow.}}∷ goe, {{ls}}el vvhat{{ls}}oeuer thou ha{{ls}}t, and giue to the poore, and thou {{ls}}halt haue trea{{ls}}ure in heauen: and come, folovv me. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=22}} Who being {{ls}}troken {{ls}}ad at the vvord, vvent avvay {{ls}}orovvful. for he had many po{{ls}}{{ls}}e{{ls}}sions. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=23}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} looking about, {{ls}}aith to his Di{{ls}}ciples, Hovv hardly {{ls}}hal they that haue money, enter into the kingdom of God! {{verse|chapter=10|verse=24}} And the Di{{ls}}ciples vvere a{{ls}}tonied at his vvordes. But {{sc|Iesvs}} againe an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aith to them, Children, hovv hard is it for them that tru{{ls}}t in money, to enter into the kingdom of God! {{verse|chapter=10|verse=25}} It is ea{{ls}}ier for a camel to pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e through a nedels eie, then for {{sup|‖}} a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=26}} VVho marueled more, {{ls}}aying to them {{ls}}elues, And vvho can be {{ls}}aued? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=27}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} beholding them, {{ls}}aith, VVith men it is impo{{ls}}sibile: but not vvith God. for al things are po{{ls}}sible vvith God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=28}} And Peter began to {{ls}}ay vnto him, Behold, vve haue left al things, and haue folovved thee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=29}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Exceding happie be they that can for{{ls}}ake their temporal things for religion.}}∷ Amen I {{ls}}ay to you, there is no man vvhich hath left hou{{ls}}e, or brethren, or {{ls}}i{{ls}}ters, or father, or mother, or children, or landes for me and for the Go{{ls}}pel: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=30}} that {{ls}}hal not receiue {{sup|‖}} an hundred times {{ls}}o much novv in this time: hou{{ls}}es, and brethren, and {{ls}}i{{ls}}ters, and mothers, and children, and landes, vvith per{{ls}}ecutions: and in the vvorld to come life euerla{{ls}}ting. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=31}} But {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 19, 30. Lu. 13, 30.''}}* many that are fir{{ls}}t, {{ls}}hal be la{{ls}}t: and the la{{ls}}t, fir{{ls}}t.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=32}} And they vvere in the vvay going vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem: and {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent before them, and they vvere a{{ls}}tonied: and folovving vvere afraid. And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 17. Lu. 18, 31.''}}* taking againe the Tvvelue, he began to tel them the things that {{ls}}hould befal him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=33}} That, behold vve goe vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem, and the Sonne of man {{ls}}hal be betrayed to the cheefe Prie{{ls}}tes, and to the Scribes and Auncients, and they {{ls}}hal condemne him to death, and {{ls}}hal deliuer him to the Gentiles, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=34}} and they {{ls}}hal mocke him, and {{ls}}pit on him, and {{ls}}courge him, and kil him, and the third day he {{ls}}hal ri{{ls}}e againe.
